statement: What the code does, and no more: an Entity never co-signs the expiry of a hold whose secret the chain showed at a height at or before the hold's deadline height (`revealed_on_chain`, for good, no wait lifts it, the payee's way is a dispute; beside `reveal_unknown`, a hash the Entity forwarded and cannot rule on yet, which is retryable). The Entity keeps the lowest height each hashlock was shown at, in whatever order it hears the events, only for a hashlock a hold (committed, proposed or queued) or a paybook entry of its own names, so strangers who call `revealSecret` with any bytes grow nothing. The comparison is by height. It is NOT the contract's: DeltaTransformer.sol (289-299) compares a block timestamp with the lock's second plus slack, so a secret shown up to floor(slack / blockSeconds) heights past the deadline height may still pay on chain while this rule lets the expiry stand (the test titled 'pays nothing' pins only that the code does not refuse a height past the deadline; it is not a claim about the chain). The expiry gate view > deadline + reserve covers the slack only by the size of the reserve. NOT covered, owed to the next PR (it gates the Sepolia value run): (1) the slack, and (2) a late lock: a hashlock the chain showed before any hold or entry names it is never kept, so a lock made after that reveal is neither refused nor claimed and pays by the registry. The close is one rule, the registry read at the decision: when the Entity accepts or forwards a lock, and when it decides an expiry co-sign, the node reads hashToTimestamp(hashlock) at the view block and compares it with deadlineSeconds(hold.deadline) + slack exactly as the contract does (a nonzero value at or before that bound means the lock is paid: refuse the lock, refuse the expiry, claim upstream), pinned by a forge vector at the exact second and one past it; a pending read freezes the decision, not the Account's other frames; a failed read is a fault for that Account only; shown entries are dropped once nothing names the hashlock and its deadline plus slack has passed.
source: coordinator relay 10-03 01:55 (never co-sign expiry of a hash whose hashToTimestamp at depth <= deadline); DeltaTransformer.sol revealSecret; coordinator relay 10-03 04:11 (spec compare of 176: D1 slack, D2 reserve, D3 late lock)

killers.name: R-REVEAL-BACKSTOP an Entity co-signs no expiry of a hold whose secret the chain showed by its deadline
R-REVEAL-BACKSTOP the Entity keeps the lowest height a secret was shown at, in any hearing order
R-REVEAL-BACKSTOP a secret no hold or entry of the Entity names is not kept, however many show
R-REVEAL-BACKSTOP a secret heard again once its hold exists is kept, whatever was heard before it
R-REVEAL-BACKSTOP a hold in a proposed frame or a queued lock is named too
R-REVEAL-BACKSTOP an expiry is refused for a hold whose secret was shown at or before its deadline
R-REVEAL-BACKSTOP a secret shown after the deadline pays nothing: the expiry stands
R-REVEAL-BACKSTOP the expiry of a hold nobody showed the secret of, or of another hashlock's, stands
R-REVEAL-BACKSTOP the refusal is for good: no wait lifts it, so the payee's way is a dispute
